generatedProse.concept-context: In sport and exercise science, the same shows up on one assignment, such as a report on training load. You might map the factors first, try both a physiological and a coaching angle, and read each study for what its data could also imply. The methods pull together on the single task.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport science students write the same report on recovery. One lists a few studies and summarises each in turn. The other maps the factors, develops two possible explanations and keeps the stronger, then reads each study for links its authors missed. The second report shows real analysis, because the methods worked as one.
generatedProse.summary: In sport and exercise science, working creatively means using all three methods on one task. You map the factors, try more than one explanation and adapt, and read studies for what their data could also mean. Used together across your modules, they make your sport science work stronger.

check.body: A student plans an essay with a mind map, tries two different arguments, drops the weaker one, and reads each source for what it could mean. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the three creative methods are working together as one way of working on a single task.
_items.feedback: Yes. Mapping, flexible thinking and imaginative reading are all in play at once.

_items.text: That the student used only one creative method and ignored the rest.
_items.feedback: Look again: mapping, flexible thinking and imaginative reading all appear.

_items.text: That mind mapping cannot be combined with other methods.
_items.feedback: The example shows mapping combined with the other two methods.

_items.text: That creativity belongs only at the planning stage of an essay.
_items.feedback: Creativity runs on here from planning through to reading the sources.
